newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds pared midday losses to end a touch down after a seesaw trading session dominated by a slew of German and U.S. data.
Bonds dipped sharply in line with bunds in early morning following the release of stronger-than-expected German M3 figures for August.
The German money supply number bumped up to an annualised 8.7 percent in August from 8.6 pct in July, surprising analysts, who had forecast a slowdown in money supply growth to 8.0 pct.
But guilder debt quickly regained much lost ground, helped by German Ifo business climate figures in line with forecasts.
The Munich-based research institute reported a modest rise in its August business climate index to 94.4 from a revised 94.0 in July.
Dealers said they did not see the M3 jump as a structural problem and foresaw no changes to the policy outlook.
"Germany is still heading for its targets, a one-off monthly figure is not a problem," one dealer said.
Another dealer said buyers were quick to emerge after the M3 dip, adding institutionals looking for bargains were supporting the market.
There had been many players who had missed out on the final rally which cut the yield on the 10-year benchmark to its current 6.04 percent from a previous 6.25 percent or so, one dealer said.
"They missed out on 20 basis points and are looking to recoup," he said.
Other dealers agreed the market was well-supported with guilder debt holding up well against bunds.
"Dutch inflation is a little higher than Germany's, so fundamentally guilder debt is a trifle overvalued," one said, but added even so scope remained for the yield gap to widen.
